texts: Write a doha about the way a fish seeks water and a lamp reaches into the dark, instinctive and without lessons, to show that the pull between two hearts is something no pundit or professor can explain.
As the fish turns to water and the lamp to the night, so two hearts turn to each other, untaught and unafraid.
lamp, fish, tender hearts
My grandparents never went past primary school, yet after fifty years he still keeps a lamp lit till she's home, and she still brings him his favourite fish curry.
doha pls, fish needs water, lamp needs night, that's how i feel about her
My nani's prayer beads are always in her lap, but the moment nana walks in, her eyes leave the beads and light up, every single time.
The beads slip through her fingers, yet her heart has already run to greet him.
prayer beads, tender heart

Write a doha about an old woman who has counted her prayer beads for decades and read every sacred text, yet whose heart is moved most by a simple glance from her husband, something no teaching ever prepared her for.
doha: prayer beads can't explain what i feel for her, just saying
Scholars have mastered every lesson, yet stand like children before the first flutter of the heart.
My uncle is a renowned professor of poetry who still turns shy and clumsy whenever the woman he likes walks into the staff room.
Please compose a doha about a brilliant man of learning who can analyse every poem about romance yet is lost and speechless when his own heart is touched, proving that this feeling has no tutor.
doha: smartest guy in the world, totally clueless when it comes to the heart
heart beyond learning

Compose a doha about a moth that dives toward its beloved without being taught or advised, a creature that never studied devotion yet gives itself entirely, showing that the heart's deepest pull needs no instruction.
doha: moth who just goes for it, no manual needed lol
moth, selfless devotion
My little cousin trails after her older brother everywhere like a moth, never minding when he shoos her away, and nobody ever told her to adore him like that.
Untaught, the moth flies to its beloved, and finds in that flight the whole of what it knew.
Every evening my husband used to row across to my village in his little boat with a lamp tied at the front, just to sit with me for an hour, and that was the whole of our courtship.
boat, lamp, sweetheart
need a doha about rowing a boat at night with a lamp to meet someone special
Through the dark crossing the lamp-lit boat comes toward me, and my heart has long since arrived.
Write a doha about a young man who rows his boat across the dark water each night, a lamp swaying beside him, driven by nothing but the longing in his heart, which no mentor ever taught him to feel.
need a doha about affection that nobody can teach
No master gave the heart its tenderness; it opened by itself, and was never the same again.
Write a doha about the deepest kind of affection, which no professor can instruct and no scripture can fully describe, and which arrives on its own to change a person's heart for good.
affection unlearned
My mother says no one taught her how to adore me; she just did, the moment the nurse put me in her arms.
I memorised dozens of romantic poems for school and thought I understood them, until I met someone and could barely say a word.
feelings beyond learning
A thousand verses read, and still the heart stammers at its first real longing.
doha about falling for someone for real
Compose a doha about the gap between reading about romance and actually feeling it, and how all our cleverness fails us in the moment when a single glance rearranges the whole heart.
My brother has a doctorate in literature and writes brilliantly about romance, but he still can't tell the girl he's crazy about how he feels.

Write a doha about a learned man who can explain affection in a hundred clever ways but cannot feel it, and a simple villager who feels it fully without saying anything, showing that the heart is not taught but awakened.
doha: professors don't know the first thing about the heart
feeling over knowledge
The learned talk of tenderness, the tender say nothing, and only the silent are understood.
need a doha for feelings i can't explain to anyone
The heart has no school and no syllabus; it opens, and there is no closing it.
wordless affection
Please write a doha about the kind of feeling that arrives without invitation, cannot be put into words or captured in lessons, and changes a person more deeply than any wisdom ever could.
I can't tell you why I'm devoted to my wife; I just know that when I'm with her, I feel like I've finally understood something.
doha: potter and his clay but really about tenderness

Compose a doha about a potter who shapes each vessel with gentle hands and a full heart, to show that tenderness is no skill taught by masters but a feeling that flows through the fingers of one who cares.
The potter's gentleness lives in his fingers, not in his learning; clay knows it, and so does the heart.
My grandfather, a potter, made a new set of cups for my grandmother every anniversary and said that affection isn't studied, it's made.
potter, clay, tenderness
unteachable feelings
doha: nobody can teach you how to care for someone
My nephew asked me what it means to adore someone, and I couldn't answer in words, so I just took his hand.
Compose a doha about the kind of closeness that no school can teach and no scholar can explain, understood in a moment between two hearts, and that changes how one sees everything afterwards.
Two hearts, one glance, and the whole of learning falls silent.
doha: fish and water, lamp and night, that's me and her

Write a doha about the bond between a lamp and the dark it brightens, a fish and the water it swims in, so natural it needs no explanation, showing that devotion between two hearts can't be studied, only lived.
My wife and I have been together thirty years, we move around each other like a fish in water, and when she walks into the room I still light up like a lamp.
The fish knows its water without knowing, the lamp its night; so the heart knows its own.
lamp, fish, soulmates
moth, wholehearted devotion
doha about a moth who gives everything for who it adores
My friend quit his job and moved cities just to be near the woman he cares about, like a moth, and says no one could have prepared him for this.
The moth dives to its beloved with no thought of itself, and calls that the whole of living.
Compose a doha about a moth that gives itself wholly to the one it adores without hesitation, showing that this devotion is something the heart simply knows and no study could ever teach.
Fish to water, sandalwood to fragrance: so the heart goes to its beloved, unlearned.
doha: fish and sandalwood and falling for someone
My uncle, a fisherman, gave my aunt a sandalwood bangle on their first anniversary and she still wears it fifty years later.
fish, sandalwood, sweethearts
Write a doha about a fisherman who gives the woman he adores a piece of sandalwood and says nothing, because tenderness is not taught but quietly felt, like fragrance, and both of them know.

Compose a doha about a lamp that burns and sandalwood that gives its fragrance, both giving themselves without being asked, a picture of devotion between two people that is natural and generous and cannot be taught.
Lamp and sandalwood give themselves away and ask no price, and need no teacher.
lamp, sandalwood, giving heart
Every evening my mother lights a lamp and rubs sandalwood on my father's forehead, a small ritual that nobody taught her; it's simply her way of saying she cares.
doha: lamp and sandalwood, how love gives
This is the one lesson that cannot be taught, only caught.
Write a doha about affection that is found not in study but in living, which touches a simple person as deeply as the wisest scholar and humbles them equally.
doha: you can't study your way into feeling something
I watched my grandparents hold hands on their evening walk, both in their eighties, and thought no education could replace what they have.
unlearned tenderness
The moth knows nothing of scholarship, yet understands the whole of devotion.
Compose a doha about a moth that has never studied anything yet knows tenderness completely, giving itself to what it adores, a reminder that the heart holds a knowledge no learning can supply.
moth, wholehearted
My daughter throws herself into every friendship like a moth, gets hurt, and does it all again, and I envy that she never learned to hold back.
doha: moth knows how to care without any lessons
Write a doha about a fish that needs no teaching to find its way home to the water, and cannot live without it, a picture of how the heart knows its beloved without being told.
The fish knows its water as the heart knows its own, without a single lesson.
My father has little education, but every Sunday he catches an extra fish just to bring home my mother's favourite dish, and that is the only lesson in romance I've needed.
fish, devotion
doha: fish and water, nobody teaches that
Compose a doha about a young man walking through a roaring market seeing only the girl he adores, deaf to the shouting and blind to the goods, because his heart is so full that nothing else exists.
In the market's thousand voices, the heart hears only one.
doha: market crowds but i only see her lol
I was buying vegetables at the market last week when I spotted her across the crowd and forgot everything I came for.
market, sweetheart
doha: sandalwood and how real caring gives without being taught

Write a doha about sandalwood that gives its fragrance freely to everything it touches without a single lesson, showing that real affection gives itself naturally and is not learned from any scholar or teacher.
sandalwood, tenderness
My grandmother hands out sandalwood paste to every neighbour at festival time, her own quiet way of caring, which nobody taught her.
Sandalwood gives its fragrance as the heart gives itself: freely, wholly, unlearned.
Tree and sandalwood share one soil, roots entwined, and the heart needs no teaching.
tree, sandalwood, two hearts
My parents met under a sandalwood tree in our village and say they knew straight away, though neither has ever been able to explain it.
doha: sandalwood tree and falling for someone
Compose a doha about a sandalwood tree that offers its fragrance to everything around it, a picture of generous, natural affection, which grows like the tree itself with no school to teach it.
Write a doha about a devotee who sits under a tree with prayer beads, only to find that no study taught him what one tender moment of the heart revealed, the only knowledge that matters.
tree, prayer beads, tenderness
My grandmother sits under the tree with her prayer beads every evening, humming and smiling, and I realised she's not praying so much as adoring.
doha: tree and prayer beads and a full heart
Under the tree the beads fall still, for the heart has taught what counting never could.
Every morning my father rowed my mother across the river to her work in his old boat, and in all those years neither of them ever once said the words.
A boat across the river and two hearts that never spoke; this is the whole language of devotion.
doha: boat, silent affection
boat, unspoken devotion
Write a doha about a boatman who rows his beloved across the water every day without a word, showing that tenderness is not taught by scholars but lives quietly in small daily acts.
Last year I asked my grandfather how he knew he wanted to marry my grandmother, and he smiled and said you don't learn it, you just wake up and it's there.
affection, unlearned
doha: caring for someone is beyond words
Learning ends where the heart begins, for the heart speaks a language no study has learned.
Please write a doha about the way deep affection arrives without any explanation and cannot be grasped by study, so that the simple heart that feels it knows more than the scholar who analyses it.
I met my husband at a vegetable stall in the market, we spoke for five minutes, and I knew that nobody had needed to teach me anything.
In the market's noise two hearts met, and the rest was silence.
doha: met my person at the market, still cant explain it
market, first glance
Compose a doha about two strangers who meet in a noisy market and are taken by each other in a single glance, an experience no study could prepare them for and no words could capture.
The potter's tenderness lives in his hands, shaping clay without a lesson.
potter, caring hands
My grandfather the potter made a new vessel for my grandmother on every birthday, and told me affection isn't taught, it's made.
Write a doha about a potter who shapes each vessel with his whole heart, putting care into every curve, to show that real devotion can't be learned from scholars but is felt in the hands.
doha: potter's care for his work
Compose a doha about how the learned can know every scripture and still miss tenderness, while the unlettered person who opens his heart understands the whole of existence in that one feeling.
doha: caring isn't something you study lol
heart over study
My grandmother never went to school, but she always knew exactly what to say to every heart that came to her in need.
Not learning but tenderness brings the last of wisdom.

Write a doha about a potter who turns his prayer beads while the clay dries, discovering that all the rituals and study in the world are nothing next to the tenderness he feels for his work and his family.
potter, prayer beads, tenderness
My uncle the potter hummed with his prayer beads and shaped clay so gently that you could tell what he truly worshipped was the act of caring.
doha: potter with prayer beads, what matters most is the heart
Beads and clay in his hands, and a heart overflowing with what he never studied.
Compose a doha about a person who counts his prayer beads year after year only to learn that all the counting was a path to tenderness, which cannot be counted or taught, only felt in the heart.
prayer beads, tender heart
I spent years chanting with my prayer beads, and only the day my child was born did I understand what the chanting was reaching for.
doha: prayer beads can't teach you how to feel
The beads can only count; tenderness is what the counting was meant to reach.
My grandfather took my grandmother to the market in his boat every morning for fifty years, and I think that was his way of telling her he adored her.
Write a doha about a man who rows his sweetheart across the water to the market each day for decades, to show that devotion is made of simple, unspoken daily acts that no teacher could ever instruct.
boat, market, devotion
A boat to the market each dawn, and a silence full of tenderness.
doha: rowing across to the market every day for the person i care about
My grandfather held my grandmother's hand with one hand and turned his prayer beads with the other, and I used to find it funny, but now I understand which one was his real prayer.
Compose a doha about a man who turns prayer beads with one hand and holds his beloved's hand with the other, understanding that affection is the only prayer that needs no teacher.
doha: prayer beads in one hand, holding hands with the other
One hand on the beads, one in the beloved's; and the second is the true prayer.
prayer beads, holding hands

Write a doha about how the heart has no teacher and no school, how this feeling simply arrives and fills a person so completely that the learned and the unlearned stand equal before it, lost in the same wonder.
The heart is a school with no teacher and no end.
heart, no teacher
doha about falling for someone
I fell for her last winter without even meaning to, and nothing I had studied or been told could have prepared me for how it felt.
My husband and I met on a boat crossing to the island for work and have never been apart since, though neither of us believed in romance before.
Compose a doha about two strangers who meet on a boat crossing and are drawn together in a single glance, an experience that no study could prepare them for and no teacher could explain.
On the boat two hearts met, and the water carried them past every lesson.
boat, first glance
doha: met on a boat, instant spark
I bought sandalwood at the market for my girlfriend's birthday and the seller smiled and said you clearly never needed to be taught how to adore someone.
market, sandalwood, girlfriend

Write a doha about a young man who buys sandalwood at the market for the woman he adores, his heart so full that he needs no instruction on how to show it, showing that real feeling gives from the heart.
doha: sandalwood from the market for my girl
Through the market's din he carries sandalwood to his beloved, with only the heart for a teacher.
My grandmother says the first time my grandfather the potter held her hand it felt like clay warmed by the sun, and she knew without being told.

Compose a doha about a potter whose hands shape clay with the same tenderness he shows his beloved, a picture of care that no teacher could instruct and no scholar could explain, but which the heart simply knows.
doha: potter's hands, gentle with clay and with her
potter, gentle hands
The hands that shape the clay hold the beloved, and tenderness needs no lesson.
Compose a doha about a fish and a lamp at night, each faithful to its own nature, as a devoted heart is faithful to the beloved without needing a lesson, since the heart holds its own knowledge.
doha: lamp and fish, caring that comes naturally
lamp, fish, devotion
The fish is true to the water, the lamp to its flame, the heart to its beloved, and none was taught.
Since he married my mother, my father has fished at dusk by lamp every day and brings back the fish she likes best, and has never said a word about it.
feelings beyond study
No teacher ever gave this lesson, yet every heart knows it by heart.

Write a doha about the experience of deep affection, which no study can give and no scholar can describe, and which makes the learned and the unlearned equal, humbled by the same overwhelming feeling.
doha pls on real feelings
My brother is a professor of literature, but at his own wedding he cried like a child because nothing he studied had prepared him for what he felt.
Not a word of learning remains once the heart has been touched; it simply knows.
I thought I understood affection from all the stories I'd heard, and then my daughter was born and I realised I'd known nothing.
heart beyond learning
doha about how caring is something you feel not learn

Compose a doha about the way real tenderness cannot be taught by anyone, how it arrives suddenly and teaches itself to the heart, leaving the person forever changed and unable to explain what has happened.
The moth never studied devotion, yet adores with its whole being.
moth, devotion
Write a doha about a moth that has never been taught how to care yet gives itself entirely to the one it adores, showing that this is not a lesson but a call that the heart simply answers.
My neighbour's son follows his sweetheart everywhere like a moth, and no one in the village has ever seen anyone so devoted.
doha: moth's devotion needs no teacher
potter, sandalwood, tenderness
My uncle the potter pressed a little sandalwood paste into every clay vessel he made for my aunt, and she says it was the most beautiful thing anyone ever did for her.
doha: potter + sandalwood, affection in the little things
Compose a doha about a potter who infuses each vessel with sandalwood and tenderness for his beloved, showing that devotion is expressed through small acts which no scholar could teach.
Clay shaped with sandalwood and tenderness: this is the language of the heart.
The fisherman's boat knows only one shore: the beloved waiting in the evening.
Write a doha about a fisherman who rows his boat home every evening not for the catch but for the one waiting for him, a picture of devotion that no teacher instructed and no scholar could describe.
doha: fisherman rowing his boat home to his sweetheart
fish, boat, sweetheart
My grandfather sailed out in his boat for fish every morning and always came back by evening because he said my grandmother would be waiting.
My parents planted a sandalwood tree on their wedding day and still sit beside it every evening, saying nothing, and it's the most real thing I've ever seen.
Compose a doha about a couple sitting beside a sandalwood tree planted at their wedding, their bond as steady and fragrant as the tree itself, an understanding that no study could teach.
doha: sandalwood tree, a couple's lasting bond
The sandalwood tree grows beside them as their devotion has grown, fragrant and unlearned.
sandalwood tree, devotion
write a doha about true love please
My grandmother lost something precious once and my grandfather spent the whole day helping her look, and when I asked him why, he said because she's mine.
The heart has no syllabus, only a lesson it learns by giving.
tenderness, unlearned

Write a doha about devotion as the one kind of wisdom that cannot be gained through study, understood only by those who have felt it, and which makes the wisest and the simplest equal in its presence.
I first saw her at the market, haggling cheerfully over vegetables, and felt something I had never read about or been taught.
doha: spotted her at the market, heart gone
Amid the market's bargaining, one glance, and the heart was bought.
market, first glance
Compose a doha about falling for someone in the middle of a noisy market, where a stranger's glance turns the whole world quiet, a feeling no scholar could teach and nobody could be prepared for.
unlearned affection

Write a doha about tenderness as the only knowledge that cannot be taught, how a simple person who feels it understands more than a scholar who has read everything, and how it transforms the one who bears it.
My shy cousin did badly in school but is the best husband I know, and his wife says he understands her in a way nobody can teach.
doha: caring doesn't need learning
The heart that cares needs no teacher; it is both student and school.
lamp, devotion
Compose a doha about a lamp that burns for its own sake, giving itself wholly to the dark, a picture of selfless devotion that no teacher could instruct and only the heart could know.
Since my father left to work abroad, my mother has kept a lamp burning at the window every night, and in five years she's never missed one.
The lamp burns for the beloved and asks nothing, and this is all devotion is.
doha: lamp burning for the one i miss

Write a doha about a fish that is devoted to its water as the heart is devoted to its beloved, without being taught or told, and how this simple natural bond is deeper knowledge than any scholar can supply.
fish, devotion
The fish needs no teacher to find its water; the heart needs no teacher to find its own.
doha: fish in water, natural affection
My father spends every Sunday fishing and my mother always packs his lunch, and I think that is just what love looks like in practice.
feelings, beyond words
doha about real affection please
No teacher can teach and no scholar can say; the heart wakes, and knows.
Compose a doha about tenderness that cannot be learned from any teacher or scholar, but is awakened in the heart when it is ready, and that changes the whole meaning of life for the one who feels it.
When my sister got engaged she said it felt like she'd always known him, though nobody had ever taught her what that meant.
well, prayer beads, tenderness
The well of the heart is deeper than the beads can count, and no teacher knows its bottom.
My grandmother draws water from the well each dawn with her prayer beads in her pocket, and says the real prayer is simply caring for everyone she meets.
doha: well and prayer beads and a kind heart

Write a doha about a person who draws water from a deep well while his prayer beads rest in his pocket, learning that the tenderness in his heart runs deeper than any ritual and cannot be taught by any teacher.
moth, unlearned devotion
Compose a doha about a moth that circles what it adores without being taught, showing that devotion is not a lesson but an instinct of the heart that gives itself entirely, even at its own cost.
doha: moth giving everything, no one teaches that
The moth was never taught to adore; it simply does, and in doing, is whole.
A friend of mine is hopelessly devoted to a woman who barely notices him, like a moth, and he says it's not a choice, it's just how his heart works.
